messages:
Alex: quick sync on RidgeCorp POC commit. They provided traffic: steady chat ~380 qps (short convos ~25 tokens) + nightly embedding bursts ~270 r/s for 45m. They want reserved GPUs + autoscale/burst controls. Can we sketch SKUs, preheat, and billing guardrails?
Sasha: chat is low-token/high-concurrency. Do they require p95<250ms?
Alex: yes p95 target = 230ms. Embeddings OK up to 2s. They also flagged BYOK and 90d logs in questionnaire.
Kevin: rough perf: our A100-equivalent gives ~42 qps/GPU for this mix when KV warm. Baseline = ceil(380/42)=10 GPUs. Recommend reserve 12 for AZ+embedding headroom, autoscale to 18 for bursts.
Kevin: optional quantized path: int8 chat -> ~1.6x throughput => baseline drops to 7 GPUs but we need quality review.
Sasha: propose two quote paths in proposal: (1) conservative A100: 12 reserved, autoscale 18, 12mo with 20% discount; (2) quantized lean: 7 reserved, autoscale 14, 12mo with 27% discount + quality SLA clause. Add H100 option as premium.
Maria: security note: BYOK ok via AWS KMS integration, will draft questionnaire answers. Need to confirm whether they want cross-region key replication or separate keys per region.
Kevin: preheat plan: staged warm to build KV cache and kernels. Steps: 1) 10% traffic 30m canary, 2) 50% 1h, 3) full ramp. Use smoke harness to check p95 at each stage. Snippet we run for cache warm: for i in 1..3600; curl -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' $ENDPOINT; sleep 1
deploy-bot: preheat canary result: p95=225ms, p99=480ms, canary healthy :white_check_mark:
Alex: billing guardrails question: can we cap daily burst spend and apply burst credits?
Kevin: yes. Implement credits_per_gpu_per_day (e.g., 900s) and throttle or fallback when exhausted. Example policy: credits:900s, fallback model chat-small-quantized, throttle_after_credits=true. We'll include alerting on overage.
Sasha: action items: @kevin produce SKU numbers for A100/H100/quantized + preheat runbook; @sasha draft 6mo vs 12mo language and upgrade/true-up mechanics; @maria finish security answers; @alex request hourly spike CSVs from customer. Reconvene after Kevin posts numbers.
